extracted.intended_audience: practitioners before the USPTO; attorneys/respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings; OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing reciprocal discipline proceedings under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including notice/response requirements, grounds for suspension, publication/notification, compliance while suspended, and reinstatement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to contest under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' informed Respondent that the OED Director had filed a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' requesting suspension; the Notice and Order directed that if Respondent seeks to contest imposition of his suspension pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), Respondent shall file, within 40 days, a response containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that the imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania would be unwarranted based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file a timely response with information establishing a genuine issue of material fact permits the Director to determine there is no genuine issue and to impose reciprocal discipline. The 40-day deadline and the requirement that the response contain 'all information' relevant to establishing a genuine issue are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's determination under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Respondent does not establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the USPTO Director may determine (1) there is no genuine issue of material fact and (2) that suspension from practice before the USPTO is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director's two-fold determination (no genuine issue; suspension appropriate) is the basis for entering a final order of reciprocal discipline where the respondent fails to meet the § 11.24(d) showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for discipline: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent was suspended for violation of the ethical standard set out in 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order treats the referenced § 10.23 provisions as the USPTO ethical standards implicated by the state court suspension; the Order also cites authority for action (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59).

rubrics_metrics.name: State professional conduct violations as basis for reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court of Pennsylvania suspended Respondent for violating that jurisdiction's Rules of Professional Conduct 3.1, 3.3(a)(1), 4.1(a), 8.2(a), 8.4(c), and 8.4(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies the factual basis cited by the state court: misconduct in civil litigation wherein he represented himself and made allegations in pleadings accusing a judge of improper and illegal activity without offering evidence for those allegations. Those state-law findings support the reciprocal USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension terms and compliance while suspended (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office for a period of five (5) years; Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while suspended; Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date this Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after the date this Final Order is signed for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order sets the suspension duration and requires adherence to the suspension-related obligations in § 11.58 (e.g., notice to clients, withdrawal, safekeeping of files — as detailed in § 11.58 itself). It also allows a narrow, time-limited recognition to permit actions necessary to comply with § 11.58(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish this Final Order; the OED Director shall publish the following notice in the Official Gazette (Notice of Suspension) and, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted to practice, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (URL provided) and published in the Official Gazette. The Order includes text for the Official Gazette notice and instructs OED to provide broader notice to relevant agencies and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure obligation (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order requires adherence to the reinstatement rules in § 11.60 (procedural requirements, evidence of rehabilitation, compliance with conditions) when seeking readmission to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirements for Final Order (37 C.F.R. § 11.11 reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order was mailed first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Respondent at the following most recent address provided to OED pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service of disciplinary orders follows the address-provision and service rules in § 11.11; the certificate of service documents mailing and date.
